Update this Next.js application to use Google Cloud Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials (ADC) instead of a Google AI Studio API key (GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY).
Please do the following:
1. Update Dependencies: Replace @google/generative-ai (or update @google/genai) with the official @google-cloud/vertexai SDK (or configure @google/genai with vertexai: true).

4. Update Model Initialization: Initialize the Vertex AI client using process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and ensure all Gemini calls run strictly on the server side."

content.text:
Gemini now runs on Vertex AI using Application Default Credentials (ADC), with no API key anywhere. Typecheck passes, but I haven't made a live call because no Google Cloud project is set yet.

**To make it work locally**, run these, then put your project ID in `.env.local`:
```
gcloud auth application-default login
GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<your-project-id>
```
Then `node scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs` checks it end to end.

What changed:
- **No new dependency.** I kept `@google/genai` and set `vertexai: true` with project and location, instead of adding `@google-cloud/vertexai`. That's one of the two options you listed, and it means no other code had to change.
- `src/lib/gemini/client.ts` and `scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs` no longer pass `apiKey`. The SDK finds your ADC credentials on its own.
- `src/lib/env.ts`, `.env.example` and `.env.local`: `GEMINI_API_KEY` is replaced by `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (required) and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` (defaults to `us-central1`).
- `SPEC.md` and `docs/hang-notes.md` now describe the new setup.
- **Server-only:** this was already true. The Gemini client imports `server-only`, so the build fails if browser code ever imports it.

The old `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env.local` wasn't a real API key. It looked like a short-lived Google sign-in token (it started with `ya29.`), which is probably why it kept failing. It's gone now.

Your earlier changes to `src/lib/http.ts` (the friendly out-of-quota error) are still there. I didn't commit anything.
OMG IT WORKS CAN YOU COMMIT PUSH AND MERGE
I'll follow the repo workflow: check for a trail, run `entire review`, then commit and push.

Reviewing jerry/vertex-ai vs origin/main: 1 commit, 7 files changed, 0 uncommitted
Running review with claude-code...
# claude-code review

Effort level: no level was given, so this ran at medium, the level you used last time. Typing a level (for example `/code-review high`) changes it.

request changes: switching to Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials breaks Gemini in production, because the Docker deployment has no way to get those credentials.

- [high] `docker-compose.yml:4` / `src/lib/gemini/client.ts:12`: The client now runs `new GoogleGenAI({ vertexai: true, project, location })` and relies on Application Default Credentials, which come from `gcloud auth application-default login`. The production `web` container only gets `env_file: .env.production`. It has no gcloud credentials, no mounted service-account JSON and no `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. On the Vultr VPS, every Gemini call (discovery, adaptation, parsing, vision) will fail with an auth error, while `/api/health` still reports ok. Fix: mount a service-account key into the container, set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` in compose, and add it to the SPEC env table, `.env.example` and hang-notes step 4.
- [medium] `src/lib/http.ts:52`: The new mapping of 429 to `RATE_LIMITED` is only in `ndjsonResponse`. `handleRouteError` still turns a Gemini `ApiError` with status 429 into `INTERNAL` "Something went wrong" (HTTP 500). Routes that call Gemini without streaming (adapt, via `src/server/recipes/adapt.ts`, and parse) therefore still show a generic 500 when quota runs out. Fix: put the 429 check in one shared helper, call it from both `handleRouteError` and `ndjsonResponse`, and return status 429.
- [low] `src/lib/http.ts:83`: The check `(err as { status?: number })?.status === 429` matches any error that has a `status` field of 429, not just Gemini's. Any other upstream error with that shape would be reported to the user as "The AI service is out of quota". Fix: test `err instanceof ApiError` from `@google/genai` before checking `status`.
- [low] `src/lib/env.ts:16`: The default `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` is `us-central1`, and I didn't confirm that `gemini-3.8-flash` is served there. Recent Gemini models on Vertex are often only on the `global` endpoint, which would make every call fail with a "model not found" error under the default config. Fix: check which regions the model is available in, and switch the default to `global` if needed (in `.env.example` and the smoke script too).
- [low] `src/lib/env.ts:16`: `z.string().default('us-central1')` only applies the default when the variable is missing. A blank `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=` line in an env file passes `''` through to the SDK, so the configured region is wrong. Fix: use `z.string().min(1).default('us-central1')` or treat an empty string as missing.
- [low] `src/lib/http.ts:83`: The new `RATE_LIMITED` branch in `ndjsonResponse` has no test. Fix: add one unit test where the producer throws `{ status: 429 }` and assert the stream emits `code: 'RATE_LIMITED'`.
- [low] `SPEC.md:1887`: The docs still assume Gemini API (AI Studio) billing and terms: "the 5k free grounded queries" here, and the "Gemini API Additional Terms" grounding item in `docs/hang-notes.md`. Vertex grounding has different pricing and terms, so the cost and compliance assumptions are now out of date. Fix: update those entries for Vertex AI.

- [Google Cloud CLI](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install) (`gcloud --version`), used to sign in to Vertex AI for Gemini
- Access to the team's Google Cloud project: ask the project owner to grant your Google account the **Vertex AI User** role (`roles/aiplatform.user`)

## Setup

```bash
npm install
```

This also runs `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (`postinstall`), which copies the MediaPipe and zxing WASM binaries into `public/` so the browser loads them locally instead of from a CDN.

### Environment variables

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

Fill in the values (ask a teammate for the shared Auth0, database and barcode keys). See `SPEC.md` §8 for the full list.

### Gemini (Vertex AI)

Gemini runs on Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials (ADC), so there is no Gemini API key. Each developer signs in with their own Google account:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default login
gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project <PROJECT_ID>
```

Then set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<PROJECT_ID>` in `.env.local` (`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` defaults to `us-central1`). Check it works with:

```bash
node --env-file=.env.local scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs
```

### Database

```bash
npm run migrate
```

## Running locally

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

- Cook mode can run against fixtures by setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOK_FIXTURES=true`.
- `/api/tts` uses ElevenLabs when `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is set; without it, voice falls back to the browser's built-in speech.

## Deployment

Production runs with `docker compose up -d --build` on the VPS. The server can't sign in through a browser, so it uses a service-account key:

1. Create a service account with the **Vertex AI User** role and download its key as `gcp-sa.json`.
2. Copy it next to `docker-compose.yml` on the server (`chmod 600`). It is gitignored; never commit or share it.
3. Put `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` in `.env.production`. `docker-compose.yml` mounts the key and sets `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.

The deploy setup is fine. The container just isn't seeing `global`. These are the likely causes, most likely first:

1. **The containers weren't recreated.** `env_file` is only read when a container is created. `docker compose restart`, or an `up -d --build` that finds nothing changed, keeps the old environment. Prod also runs 4 replicas behind Caddy, so one stale replica gives intermittent errors.
2. **`.env.production` has the line twice.** If it started as a copy of `.env.example`, it may still contain `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1` further down, and the last line wins.
3. **The line is malformed:** spaces around `=`, quotes, or Windows line endings if you edited it on your PC and copied it over.

Run this on the server to check (`cat -A` makes stray characters visible):
```sh
cd ~/hackcamp27
grep -n "GOOGLE_CLOUD" .env.production | cat -A
for i in 1 2 3 4; do docker compose exec --index $i web printenv GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION; done
```
The `grep` line should read exactly `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global$`. If you see `^M$` at the end, run `sed -i 's/\r$//' .env.production`. All 4 replicas should print `global`.

Then recreate the containers so they pick up the file:
```sh
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web
```

# Gemini issues

## Prod: 404 "Publisher model ... locations/us-central1/... gemini-3.8-flash was not found"

**Symptom:** Gemini calls fail in production with a 404 naming `locations/us-central1`. The same code works on localhost.

**Cause:** `gemini-3.8-flash` is only served on Vertex AI's `global` endpoint, not in `us-central1`. Localhost has `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global` in `.env.local`. In prod, at least one container does not see that value, so `src/lib/env.ts` falls back to its default, `us-central1`.

The service-account key is not the problem: the error names the right project, so auth worked.

`src/lib/gemini/client.ts` is the only place that creates the Gemini client, and `@google/genai` uses exactly the location we pass. So `us-central1` can only come from the container's environment or the default in `src/lib/env.ts`.

### Fix 1: code default (needs a `contract:` commit; `src/lib/**` is frozen)

In `src/lib/env.ts`:

```diff
-  GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION: z.string().min(1).catch('us-central1'), // blank line in .env also falls back
+  GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION: z.string().min(1).catch('global'), // blank line in .env also falls back
```

Commit it on its own, titled e.g. `contract: default GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION to global`, then merge and deploy (`./deploy.sh` on the server).

Optional, to see what each container actually uses: in `getClient()` in `src/lib/gemini/client.ts`, right after the client is created, add:

```ts
console.info(`[gemini] vertex project=${env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT} location=${env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION}`);
```

Then check `docker compose logs web | grep gemini`.

The docs, `.env.example` and `scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs` already default to `global` (branch `jerry/vertex-global`).

### Fix 2: check the server (works without a deploy)

On the VPS:

```sh
cd ~/hackcamp27
# Must print exactly GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global$ once. ^M$ = Windows line endings, a second line = duplicate (last one wins).
grep -n "GOOGLE_CLOUD" .env.production | cat -A
# Fix Windows line endings if needed:
sed -i 's/\r$//' .env.production
# Every replica (there are 4) must print global:
for i in 1 2 3 4; do docker compose exec --index $i web printenv GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION; done
# env_file is only read when a container is created, so recreate after any change:
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web
```

Also check for other places that could set it: `.env` next to `docker-compose.yml`, or exported shell variables (`env | grep GOOGLE`).

## Local dev reminders

- Sign in: `gcloud auth application-default login` and `gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project <PROJECT_ID>`.
- `.env.local` needs `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<PROJECT_ID>` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global` (or leave the location out once Fix 1 is merged). If you copied an older `.env.example`, it may still say `us-central1`: change it.
- Smoke test: `node --env-file=.env.local scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs`.

Request changes. The branch changes the docs to say `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` defaults to `global`, but the code still defaults to `us-central1`. Following the new README in production would cause the same 404 this branch is meant to fix.

- [high] README.md:68: The production step tells operators to set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global` "(or leave it out)". The code default has not changed: `src/lib/env.ts:27` is still `z.string().min(1).catch('us-central1')`. An operator who leaves the variable out gets `us-central1`, and every Gemini call fails with the "Publisher model ... not found" 404 that `gemini-issues.md` describes. Fix: remove "(or leave it out)" until the `contract:` commit that changes the `env.ts` default to `'global'` is merged, or land that commit with this branch.

- [medium] README.md:39: This says "`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` defaults to `global`", but the app falls back to `us-central1` (`src/lib/env.ts:27`). Only the smoke script defaults to `global`. A developer with an older `.env.local`, or with the variable unset, sees the smoke test pass while the app returns 404, and the README points them the wrong way. Fix: say it must be set to `global` until the `env.ts` default changes.

- [medium] SPEC.md:1043: The SPEC table now lists the default as `global`, while the code in frozen `src/lib/env.ts` still uses `us-central1`. CLAUDE.md says: "If the contracts and SPEC disagree, the contracts win; raise the mismatch with a human." This commit creates that mismatch instead of raising it. Fix: change SPEC in the same `contract:` commit that changes `env.ts`, or keep `us-central1` in SPEC until then.

- [low] scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs:12: `process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION ?? 'global'` does not treat an empty value as unset. The app does (`.catch(...)` on `min(1)`, with the comment "blank line in .env also falls back"). With a blank `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=` line in `.env.local`, the script passes `location: ''` to the SDK while the app uses its default. Fix: `process.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION || 'global'`.

- [low] gemini-issues.md:32: "already default to `global` (branch `jerry/vertex-global`)" names a branch that goes out of date once this merges. Line 45 also hard-codes `for i in 1 2 3 4`, which copies `replicas: 4` from `docker-compose.yml` and will be wrong if that number changes. Fix: drop the branch name, and loop over `docker compose ps -q web` instead.
